# AI Safety Research Atlas

> A source-pinned research database that connects AI-safety questions to theories, assumptions, formal results and evidence. Every record names its source and location, and every connection keeps its review state. This file tells AI agents how to use it.

Snapshot 4571dcd419e477499ca46ce8a3d785a33972a650fff46446afb7a9c16d9a22a3 (canonical commit f196efd449cdb2fa065ca6d6178f781bfcc2cafa): 1,750 records, 5,821 recorded links, 245 sources. Static files only; no login, no rate limit beyond the host's.

## Rules

- Every record and link keeps its recorded state; most are PROPOSED (AI-drafted, unreviewed). Say so when you use them.
- A link is a recorded connection, not a verified relationship. An empty path_eligibility means the link may not be chained to carry a result into another setting.
- Cite the paper and the PDF page in the record's sources, and check the paper before relying on a claim.
- Counts are indexed records, not distinct ideas or papers. Absence of a record is a gap in the atlas, not evidence that nothing exists.

## Files

- [agent/index.json](https://elshatlawy.github.io/AI-Safety-Research-Atlas-/agent/index.json): every record's id, title, type, kind, domains, state, sources and card path. Scan it to find candidates.
- agent/records/<card>.json: one record with its text, sources (paper, locator, a link that opens the PDF at the cited page), outgoing and incoming links with their state, rationale, open obligations and path eligibility, and a link to the record on the website.
- [agent/papers.json](https://elshatlawy.github.io/AI-Safety-Research-Atlas-/agent/papers.json): every source with the records drawn from it.
- [atlas_data.json](https://elshatlawy.github.io/AI-Safety-Research-Atlas-/atlas_data.json): the full public view (records, links, sources, aliases, review events) for programmatic use; [PUBLIC_BUILD_MANIFEST.json](https://elshatlawy.github.io/AI-Safety-Research-Atlas-/PUBLIC_BUILD_MANIFEST.json) has every file's hash.
- [problem_routes.json](https://elshatlawy.github.io/AI-Safety-Research-Atlas-/problem_routes.json): guided problem routes (monitoring limits; information and oversight) over existing records.

## Recipes

Record cards give each record's `type` and, for records drafted from full texts, its `kind` (for example FULLTEXT_EMPIRICAL_RESULT_CANDIDATE). Links between papers in the debate and scalable oversight batch have relation `candidate_mapping`; their `scope` starts with the proposed relation, such as "proposed SUPPORTS", "proposed CHALLENGES", "proposed CRITIQUES", "proposed EXTENDS" or "proposed ADDRESSES". A scope starting "proposed SHARES_TOPIC" marks a navigation-only link: the two records discuss the same topic and neither bears on the other's claim, so never count it as evidence.

- Theory discovery ("Which information-theoretic results are relevant to monitoring limits?"): scan titles, types and domains in agent/index.json, open the candidate cards, and follow links with relation candidate_mapping, curated_context, analogous_to or outcome_transfer. Report each link's state and scope.
- Assumption tracing ("What must hold for this claim to apply?"): open the claim's card and read links with relation application_requires or formal_statement_requires; in agent/papers.json, list the same paper's records with type ASSUMPTION or kind FULLTEXT_ASSUMPTION_CANDIDATE. List every open_obligations entry.
- Definition comparison ("Do these papers use the same definition of oversight?"): find records with type definition or DEFINITION or kind FULLTEXT_DEFINITION_CANDIDATE, then compare their text and sources. A link between two definitions is a candidate, not an identity.
- Formalization navigation ("Where is this result formalized, and what remains informal?"): read formal_statement and formal_declaration on the card and links such as paper_to_lean_semantic_match, implementation_to_formal_semantic_match, formal_statement_requires and formal_proof_uses. MACHINE_CHECKED covers the formal statement only; the informal reading stays unreviewed unless a link says HUMAN_REVIEWED. Cards list at most 40 kernel dependency links per direction; atlas_data.json has them all.
- Research-gap analysis ("Which proposed connections lack semantic or implementation evidence?"): in atlas_data.json, select links with state PROPOSED or OPEN, open questions (kind FULLTEXT_OPEN_QUESTION_CANDIDATE or type open_problem) and the links whose scope starts "proposed ADDRESSES" toward them. No link is yet eligible to carry a result into another setting.
- Evidence inspection ("What experiments support this claim, and what population was tested?"): open the claim's card and read links whose scope starts "proposed SUPPORTS", "proposed CHALLENGES" or "proposed CRITIQUES", and empirical_evidence_for links. Records with kind FULLTEXT_EMPIRICAL_RESULT_CANDIDATE or type EVIDENCE, OBSERVATION or EXPERIMENT state their setting in the text; check it at the cited PDF page.
- Learning paths ("Which concepts and results do I need to understand this research problem?"): start from problem_routes.json and follow each stage's records in order.
- Programmatic research ("Export the relevant subgraph for my tool or agent"): load atlas_data.json and select records and links by id. Keep each record's state and source_refs with whatever you export.

## Open questions and discoveries (gap-closing pilot, AI drafts)

The pilot ranked 33 open questions from the debate and scalable-oversight papers by the step of the debate safety case (Buhl et al. 2025, arXiv 2505.03989) each one affects, and recorded what later work, Lean proofs and pooled results settle. Ledger: 6 Proved, 52 Paper problem, 11 Derived, 12 Partly answered by later work, 15 Narrowed. Everything here passed two blind AI checks tested on planted errors; no person has reviewed it.

- [agent/gaps.json](https://elshatlawy.github.io/AI-Safety-Research-Atlas-/agent/gaps.json): the ranked questions with status, the safety-case steps each affects and how well supported those steps are, and the file for each question.
- agent/gaps/<id>.json: one question with its counted later-work findings (claim, setting, effect, exact quoted lines with a link to the PDF page), what remains, and the experiment package if one is drafted (agent/packages/<id>.json: hypothesis, design, outcomes and how each would be read, resources, risks).
- [agent/cards.json](https://elshatlawy.github.io/AI-Safety-Research-Atlas-/agent/cards.json): result cards for the 42 papers: each result, theorem or claim with its evidence type, the method that produced it, its stated hypotheses and assumption records, its setting (systems, task, judge, regime, scale) and a strength grade; agent/cards/<arXiv id>.json holds one paper's cards with the quoted lines behind them. Only cards whose latest check passed are listed. A theorem card's hypothesis list is marked not verified: the checks miss some dropped conditions there, so read the theorem's statement at the cited page.
- [agent/ledger.json](https://elshatlawy.github.io/AI-Safety-Research-Atlas-/agent/ledger.json): every result the pilot counts, labelled Proved, Paper problem, Derived, Answered by later work, Partly answered by later work or Narrowed.
- [agent/stress.json](https://elshatlawy.github.io/AI-Safety-Research-Atlas-/agent/stress.json): a stress test of the assumption "Training reaches equilibrium" (AF21). For each of the 15 safety-case steps that rest on it, a verdict at two weaker strengths, Local only (training ends at a point where no small change helps either debater, but a large change could; it need not be a global equilibrium) and Stops early (training stops before any equilibrium, global or local), with the finding that the error bound survives with no equilibrium if two named checks pass, backed by a Lean proof and an exhaustive census of small debate games.

Recipes:
- "Is this question still open?": find it in agent/gaps.json, then read `status`, `status_check` and the counted findings in its file. A finding settles only what its quoted setting shows.
- "Which gaps matter most for a debate safety case?": sort agent/gaps.json by `rank`; each question's `safety_case_steps` names the steps it affects, and the top-level `safety_case_steps` map gives each step's evidence label (NONE, WEAK, CONTESTED, SUPPORTED) and wording.
- "What holds, by what method, under which assumptions, and how strongly?": filter agent/cards.json by paper, grade or regime, then open the paper's file and read `assumptions` (stated hypotheses and assumption records) before carrying a result elsewhere; on theorem cards the list is not verified (`hypotheses_verified` is false), so check the theorem's own statement at the cited page.
- "What would settle this gap?": read `remaining_question` and `remaining_type` in its file; an empirical gap may carry an experiment package with hypothesis, design, sample size and cost estimates.
- "Which question should I work on next, given my role?": find your role in `blocker_labels` of agent/gaps.json (Experimenter: MEASUREMENT, Prover: PROOF, Definer: DEFINITION, Auditor: STATEMENT_MATCH, Inspector: SYSTEM_EVIDENCE, Explainer: EXPLANATION), keep the questions whose `blockers` hold that label, and take the best `rank`; its file's `blockers` give each part's next action and the words of `remaining_question` it covers (no `covers` means the whole question). Labels are AI drafts that passed two blind AI checks.
- "What did the pilot find that is not easy to find elsewhere?": read agent/ledger.json; Paper problem entries are flaws in a paper's own statements found by Lean audits.
- "What still holds if training falls short?": read agent/stress.json. `finding` states the two checks and links the Lean theorem and the census; `steps[].cells` gives each step's verdict when the assumption is loosened (ok = still stands; chk = stands if the two checks pass; bad = fails, or the failure happens; na = no longer used; op = still open) with a one-line reason. The whole grid is exported only when every cell passed its checks.

## Definition comparisons

- [definitions.json](https://elshatlawy.github.io/AI-Safety-Research-Atlas-/definitions.json): 11 concepts from the debate and scalable-oversight papers, 49 definitions set side by side (the page's Definitions tab). Each cell says what one paper's definition sets for one question and cites the exact words, in the record's quote or in further lines of the same PDF with page and lines. Cells with the same group set the same rule. AI-drafted; every cell and statement passed two blind AI checks; no person has reviewed them. Check the cells that differ before carrying a result from one row's definition to another.

## Replication tracker

- [replications.json](https://elshatlawy.github.io/AI-Safety-Research-Atlas-/replications.json): 41 questions that several debate and scalable-oversight papers test, one row per paper with its answer, finding and setting, each citing the exact words (the page's Replications tab). Of the 224 results and main claims, 23 hold in every other paper on their question, 8 conflict, 66 are mixed and 127 are tested once. AI-drafted; every entry passed two blind AI checks; no person has reviewed them. Before citing a result, check its status and the differences between settings.

## Understanding cards

- [understanding.json](https://elshatlawy.github.io/AI-Safety-Research-Atlas-/understanding.json): 248 results explained in plain words (the top of each result's page): why it matters, what it says, the key idea, what it was shown for and what it does not show, each line citing the exact words it rests on. AI-drafted; every card passed two blind AI checks; no person has reviewed them. Cite the paper's own words, not the card's.

## Support on the safety case

- [data.json](https://elshatlawy.github.io/AI-Safety-Research-Atlas-/data.json) `case.nodes`: every step of the debate safety case with `ev` (its own evidence label), `st` (1 when support reaches it) and `wait` (the steps at the bottom it still waits on). The rule (`case.flow_rule`): A step counts as supported when its own checked evidence supports it, or when it is split into sub-claims and every sub-claim and assumption under it counts as supported. Either way, every threat under it (a way the argument could fail) must be ruled out: at least one strong or two moderate results show the failure does not happen, and none shows it does. Open problems and evidence-needed notes hold nothing back. The rule only adds support: a step's own evidence label never changes. Today 2 of 45 steps count as supported and the top claim waits on 27 steps. `case.maps` lists each step's checked evidence; 7 entries are Lean proofs, whose `q` names the question the proof answers. The mappings are AI-drafted and passed two blind AI checks; no person has reviewed them.

## What would move each question

- [data.json](https://elshatlawy.github.io/AI-Safety-Research-Atlas-/data.json) `gap.questions[].blockers`: each open question's parts, each with `k` (the kind of work it waits on), `next` (the next action, drawn only from the question's `remaining_question`) and `covers` (the words of `remaining_question` the part covers; none means the whole question). `gap.blocker_labels` names each kind and the role that does it (Experimenter takes MEASUREMENT, Prover takes PROOF, Definer takes DEFINITION, Auditor takes STATEMENT_MATCH, Inspector takes SYSTEM_EVIDENCE, Explainer takes EXPLANATION). Today 33 of 33 questions are labelled: 28 measurement, 7 proof, 2 definition (a question in two parts counts under both). To pick your top item, keep the questions whose parts carry your role's kind and take the lowest `rank`; agent/gaps.json carries the same labels. The labels are AI-drafted and passed two blind AI checks; no person has reviewed them.

## What still holds if training falls short

- [data.json](https://elshatlawy.github.io/AI-Safety-Research-Atlas-/data.json) `deps.stress`: a stress test of the assumption "Training reaches equilibrium" (AF21), which the safety case states as "training reaches an approximate global equilibrium of the debate game". For each of the 15 steps that rest on it, `steps[].cells` holds a verdict at two weaker strengths, "Local only" (local), "Stops early" (early), where `v` is one of ok (still stands), chk (stands if the two checks pass), bad (fails, or the failure happens), na (no longer used), op (still open) and `why` is a one-line reason. Today 6 cells are chk. The finding (`finding`): the error bound survives with no equilibrium if two checks pass (Bob cannot do better against the final Alice; Alice's measured score clears a known bar); it is backed by a Lean proof (two_check_bound, five_eps_without_equilibrium, stackelberg_passes_checks, theorem_6_2, checks_weaker) and an exhaustive census of small debate games with no counterexample. The grid is AI-drafted and passed two blind AI checks; no person has reviewed it.

## What each Lean proof uses

- [data.json](https://elshatlawy.github.io/AI-Safety-Research-Atlas-/data.json) `deps.lean[].inputs`: for each of the 14 Lean projects, the assumptions its theorems state, ranked by how many proofs use them (`assumptions[]`: `s` the statement, `n` proofs that use it, `d` theorems given it that never use it), the ones never used (`dropped[]`), and the lemmas most of the project rests on (`lemmas[]`: `down` declarations that rest on it, `general` true when its statement names only Lean and Mathlib, `o` declarations in other projects that use it). Each theorem node carries `hy` = [assumptions used, assumptions stated] and `hx`, the statements of the ones it never uses. Today 4 of the 759 assumptions stated by 758 theorems go unused; 65 of the 526 lemmas other proofs use state pure maths; 47 lemmas already carry proofs in another project. `deps.inputs.conventions` defines `used`: a Lean metaprogram strips every argument a called lemma never uses from the proof term and checks whether the assumption still occurs, so used = false proves the theorem holds without it and used = true does not prove it is needed. Machine-established from the compiled proofs; no person has reviewed the reading.

## Credit and reuse

- [data.json](https://elshatlawy.github.io/AI-Safety-Research-Atlas-/data.json) `credit`: whose work each result builds on and how often it is reused, counted from items data.json already holds (`credit.rules`). `credit.records` maps a record index to [later results that build on it in the authors' own words, ones linked by AI comparison leads, safety-case steps that use it as evidence]; what a record builds on is its own `links` with `r` extends or depends. `ladder` ranks the most reused results and `papers` the papers; `made` credits each ledger entry to the paper whose question it takes up (`asker`) or that it is about (`in`), and `asked` lists, per paper, the open questions the atlas worked on under their strongest result. Today 97 results are reused: 33 are built on by 60 later results (37 in the authors' own words) and 67 back 91 safety-case uses; the atlas took up 27 open questions from 23 papers. The counts add no claim; the links and mappings they count passed two blind AI checks, and the atlas's own answers are AI-made and provisional.

## Shared structures

- [data.json](https://elshatlawy.github.io/AI-Safety-Research-Atlas-/data.json) `structure`: three structures results from different lanes share (game, information channel, constrained policy), each with a plain definition. `structure.records` maps a record index to its tags [structure, exact words from the paper, why in one line]; each entry of `structure.structures` lists its results by lane (`lanes`, lane index to record indices) and the assumption families its results use in two or more lanes (`shared`, family id and results per lane), where a result from one lane may carry over to another if that assumption holds there. Today: game 84 results in 7 lanes, 17 families shared across lanes; information channel 146 results in 9 lanes, 21 families shared across lanes; constrained policy 70 results in 9 lanes, 18 families shared across lanes; 92 results are about two or more and 53 about none. Tags are AI drafts from each result card's quoted passages; only those that passed two blind AI checks are shown (247 of 248 cards).

## Humans

The visual atlas is at the site root, https://elshatlawy.github.io/AI-Safety-Research-Atlas-/. Every record is a dot in the record graph at https://elshatlawy.github.io/AI-Safety-Research-Atlas-/#graph (a card's human_url opens one record there); the page can arrange the same dots by group, by kind (layers), by the year of the paper quoted, or by population with the links that bridge populations, and light what rests on a record, the results that use one assumption family, where papers agree or disagree, and the shortest chain of links between two records. graph.json carries each record's layer, col and date for the same purpose. Corrections and new sources go to the research repository through its maintainer.
